content: Norethindrone is a synthetic progestin, a type of hormone similar to the naturally occurring progesterone in the body. It is commonly prescribed to treat abnormal uterine bleeding, secondary amenorrhea (absence of menstrual periods not due to pregnancy or menopause), and endometriosis, a condition where uterine-like tissue grows outside the uterus, causing pain and irregular periods. How to Use: Take this medication orally as directed by your physician. It can be taken with or after food to minimize stomach upset. Follow the prescribed dosing schedule carefully. For conditions like secondary amenorrhea or abnormal uterine bleeding, it is typically taken once daily for 5 to 10 days during the second half of the menstrual cycle. If you have any questions about the medication or its use, consult your doctor. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, mood swings, difficulty sleeping, weight changes (gain or loss), acne, breast tenderness or swelling, changes in sexual interest, unwanted hair growth, or hair loss. Rare but serious side effects include blood clots, which may lead to heart attack, stroke, or pulmonary embolism. These risks are higher when combined with estrogen-containing products. Allergic reactions to this medication are rare but may occur. Symptoms of a severe allergic reaction include rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to norethindrone or any of its components. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you know how it affects you. Alcohol or cannabis use may exacerbate dizziness. Prolonged sun exposure may worsen melasma (dark patches on the skin). Use sunscreen and limit time in the sun. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It passes into breast milk, so caution is advised if breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Norethindrone may interact with other medications, altering its effectiveness or increasing the risk of side effects. Examples include azole antifungals (e.g., itraconazole), rifamycins (e.g., rifampin), and certain herbal products like St. John’s Wort. Always inform your doctor and pharmacist about all medications and supplements you are taking. Overdose: In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., call 911 or the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Monitoring: Regular physical exams, including blood pressure checks, breast exams, pelvic exams, and Pap smears, are recommended while using this medication. Report any unusual lumps in the breast or other concerning symptoms to your doctor immediately. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Important Notes: This medication is not suitable for use before menarche (the first menstrual period). Discontinue use at least 4 weeks before major surgery or prolonged immobilization to reduce the risk of blood clots. Some studies suggest a potential link between oral contraceptive use and an increased risk of breast or cervical cancer, though findings are inconsistent. The risk may be influenced by factors such as early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity, or first childbirth after age 30. Long-term use of oral contraceptives (5 years or more) may increase the risk of liver cancer. Always consult your healthcare provider for personalized medical advice and to address any concerns regarding this medication.
